messages:
lauren: FYI CVE-2026-1024 (libssl) just published and grype flagged it in a bunch of our base images. scan shows 45 images across ubuntu:22.04 variants and a few alpine-edge builds.
raj: ugh. severity/CVSS? which images are the highest-traffic?
lauren: CVSS 8.1. affected libs: libssl 3.x. highest traffic: rwi/runtime:prod-2025-03, rwi/dedicated-ubuntu-22.04-gpu, and the internal buildkite runner image. minimal-impact to alpine-musl runtime but openssl in alpine-edge is flagged too.
olivia: do we have any images signed with KMS-backed attestations? might be an opportunity to block promotions until rebuilds are validated.
lauren: only the release pipeline does signing right now (KMS: projects/redwood/kms/keys/release-sign). we do snapshot signing for official images but dev/test images are unsigned. thinking: rebuild + re-sign, then promote. need RBAC so only sec-release or infra-ci can approve promotions.
raj: agree. also need to check private/on-prem customer bundles — they pull specific image SHAs. notifying them asap.
lauren: quick repro of grype output attached (snippet):
```
Name: libssl3
Version: 3.0.11-1ubuntu2.4
Vulnerability: CVE-2026-1024
Severity: High
Fix: 3.0.11-1ubuntu2.5
Affected image: rwi/runtime:prod-2025-03
```
raj: timeline proposal? canary first, then broad rollout. we should avoid automated mass replace during business hours.
tim: @lauren created ticket SEC-7342 with triage checklist and canary window. link: https://redwood.internal/ops/SEC-7342
lauren: plan I propose: 1) create minimal rebuilds with patched libssl (ubuntu + alpine) 2) run unit/e2e smoke in dedicated canary pool (low-traffic) 3) if no regressions, sign with KMS and promote to staging 4) schedule weekend mass rollout for hosted clusters and queue messages for Dedicated customers 5) create advisory for Private customers with migration steps.
olivia: RBAC change: add a new role image-promoter scoped to release pipeline with mfa-required. Also add audit log webhook to push image-promotion events to long-term logs (retention 1y). Security team can review.
lauren: will open infra PR for role and webhook. need input on KMS key rotation — if we rotate key during rollout we must re-sign or ensure verification chain still works for customers.
raj: for on-prem: if customers verify signatures themselves, rotate notice must include grace period and commands to re-verify. we should also publish signed manifests per-arch.
security-bot: Vulnerability intake updated: SEC-7342 -> severity High, affected images: 45, blockers: none. Remediation owner: lauren. ETA: 72h.
lauren: action owners: lauren (rebuild + canary), olivia (RBAC + audit webhook), raj (customer comms & on-prem manifest), tim (ticket tracking + postmortem). I'll start builds now. posting build ids shortly.
raj: also add a quick smoke that exercises KV cache and long-context tokenization path — we've seen regressions with openssl ABI changes in the past.
lauren: good call. adding that to canary smoke. I'll ping infra-oncall if any latency spikes during canary.
olivia: drafting advisory template. sending to legal/compliance for signoff.
lauren: thanks all. we'll re-sync in #eng-security after canary finishes. :thumbsup:
